subject: Fwd: HelioForge — sizing request and proposal for warm reserve runway
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah@helioforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for late-stage POC

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the performance numbers. We're moving to a constrained late-stage POC next month and need help sizing a small dedicated pool + a short warm-reserve window while we finalize pricing & procurement.

Quick context: POC is expected to ramp to ~25 concurrent sessions, average seq len ~1024, burst to 40 concurrent for 2–3 hrs/day during evaluation. Attached is our rough MAU/usage spreadsheet.

Asks:
- Can Redwood provision a modest dedicated slice that would satisfy the above for 6 weeks?
- We want a short warm-reserve (soft hold) for 14 days prior to the POC start to avoid allocation churn; would that be feasible?
- Any recommendation on model/quantization to control spend while keeping latency under 350ms p50?

Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Sarah Lang
Head of ML Engineering
HelioForge

Attachments: helioforge_mau_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Kim / team,

Commercial context: HelioForge is late-stage and asking for a low-friction procurement path — they prefer a short warm reserve vs. a signed capacity commit until procurement completes. We can offer SKU-level pricing for a 6-week dedicated window, but we should avoid hard over-provisioning.

From my side, if Ops can provide a warm reserve for 14 days (i.e., nodes are flagged but not fully committed for billing unless they go live), I’ll propose a trial addendum: 6-week reserved capacity, with a 14-day warm-reserve waiver to be converted at contract signature. That reduces procurement risk for them.

I'll hold off external confirmation until we get Ops feasibility and a node-level sizing.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioForge — sizing request and proposal for warm reserve runway

SG: I support a warm-reserve approach for late-stage POCs where procurement timing is the blocker. Two asks for Ops:
1) Provide a pragmatic sizing recommendation (node count + model variant) that meets the burst profile without wasting fleet capacity.
2) Define the mechanism: how we flag nodes as warm-reserved (taint + affinity), how long we hold them, and the automatic reclaim/fallback policy.

Neha — can you run a quick availability check and propose an exact config (e.g., 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes with 2-way packing using quantized bf16-8 or 3 x H100-80GB-equivalent with 1.5x packing) and a timeline to set the warm-reserve? Also note any SLA implications.

If Ops can commit to a non-billable warm-reserve for up to 14d and give a concrete fallback plan, I will greenlight Ben to propose the trial addendum.

—Vivek
VP, Commercial Operations

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioForge — sizing request and proposal for warm reserve runway

On Sun, Nov 8, 2026 at 09:18 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Neha — can you run a quick availability check and propose an exact config ...

Checked fleet availability and did a quick run of simulated packing for the requested profile. Summary: 
- Recommended initial config: 3 x rdin-2 (H100-equivalent) nodes with 2:1 session packing using a quantized fp16/8 runtime — should achieve p50 ~220–300ms at target concurrency in our US-west zone.
- If HelioForge insists on headroom for burst to 40 concurrent, add one hot spare (4th node) as warm-reserve.
- Warm-reserve mechanics: Ops can taint 1 node per warm-reserve request and mark it as non-billable until conversion. Reclaim policy: if not converted after 14d, node is drained with 48h notice.
- Timeline: We can set taints and network routing rules within 48 hours of approval; full provisioning and QA of the dedicated slice takes ~72 hours after conversion.
- SLA notes: Warm-reserve is not covered by our standard Dedicated SLA until conversion. We'll provide performance monitoring and alerting during the reserve window.

Attachments: runway_sizing_notes.pdf (ops simulation outputs and packing assumptions)

Action items:
- Ben: confirm commercial language for warm-reserve (non-billable hold -> conversion terms).
- Kimberly: if greenlit, I will schedule the taint & routing change (48h).

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer (Capacity Planning), Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HelioForge — warm reserve and 6-week dedicated window (next steps)

Sarah / Raj — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick update from Redwood:

- Ops recommends a starting dedicated slice of 3 rdin-2 (H100-equivalent) nodes with quantized fp16/8 packing; add a 4th node as a warm-reserve if you expect regular 40-concurrent bursts.
- We can flag a single warm-reserve node as non-billable for up to 14 days prior to POC start; if you convert within that window we’ll formalize the dedicated reservation and billing will begin on conversion. If not converted, we'll drain the reserve with 48h notice.
- Timeline: Once you OK the warm-reserve, Ops will set the taint & routing rules within 48 hours. Conversion -> full dedicated provisioning and QA is ~72 hours thereafter.

Ben will propose the trial addendum language reflecting the warm-reserve mechanics and conversion terms. Neha and Ops will stand by to set the reserve once Ben gives the green light commercially.

Can you confirm (A) whether you want the 4th warm-reserve node, and (B) tentative POC start date so we can align the 14-day window?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
